To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) phenomenographic research can be used as a framework to identify and describe different ways of engaging in learning and to identify the conditions that support and constrain these ways, and that (2) critical theory can be used to understand the structural barriers that constrain students‟ engagement in higher education.

the phenomenographic and critical perspectives can be brought together in a model of academic engage ment that is sensitive to both experiential factors, such as the learning environments that students and teachers experience and structural factors that affect students‟ and teachers‟ access to learning and teaching opportunities.

(a) phenomenography and critical pedagogy perspectives can be reconciled through a focus on student engagement; and (b) student engagement is influenced by the interaction of both the structural and experiential aspects of the learning environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how students and teachers can engage in learning in a way that is meaningful to them.
the quality of students’ experiences of higher education and the factors that influence that quality.
the question of how we might improve the quality of the learning experience in higher education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
The model of academic engagement presented in this article is a way of bringing together phenomenographic and critical pedagogical perspectives on teaching and learning in Higher Education.
academic engagement is a complex and multi-faceted concept.
a critical phenomenographic approach to higher education teaching and learning is a more appropriate and useful approach than either a phenomenographic or a critical approach in isolation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phenomenography and critical pedagogy can be reconciled by a focus on the academic engagement of students in higher education.

we have developed a theoretical framework for understanding the complex and multi-faceted nature of the engagement of students in learning and teachers in teaching in higher education and that this framework can be used to inform teaching and learning practices.
the two perspectives can be combined to form a new model of academic engagement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the phenomenographic literature to develop a more detailed understanding of the ways in which structural inequality influences students‟ engagement with their studies.
the two perspectives can be brought together in ways that are mutually beneficial and that can lead to a more holistic understanding of the barriers to academic engagement.
the two perspectives have much to learn from one another and that the two can be brought together through a focus on engagement in learning and teaching.
